findings.title: deleteCache throws plain Error instead of TRPCError
findings.body: The handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps unknown errors to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) and, in production, replaces the message, so the client cannot distinguish "not yours" from a server failure, and the failure is logged/reported as a server bug. Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN", message: ... })` as the other handlers in this router do.

findings.title: Cache deletion only supports personal credentials, not team/delegation credentials
findings.body: Access is validated with `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`. Calendar credentials installed on a team have `userId = null`, and delegation credentials are in-memory with negative ids, so for those connected calendars the lookup fails and the mutation errors out. The new dropdown in SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper renders the "Delete cached data" entry for any credential that has a cache row (including team/delegation-backed ones), so users will get an "Error deleting cache" toast with no way to clear the cache. Either extend the authorization check (team membership / delegation ownership) or hide the action for those credentials.

findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
findings.body: The disconnect mutation invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`, but `deleteCacheMutation` only calls the optional `onSuccess` callback. `onSuccess` is wired to `props.onChanged`, which is optional and undefined on several call sites of SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper. In that case the success toast is shown but the UI keeps displaying the old "Cache Status / Last updated" entry until a manual refresh, making it look like deletion failed. Add `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in the mutation's onSettled/onSuccess.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is hard-coded to en-US formatting
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })` ignores the user's locale and 12h/24h time preference, so a non-US user sees MM/DD/YY and AM/PM dates inside an otherwise translated string. Use the user's locale (e.g. from `useLocale()`) / the existing date-formatting helpers instead of a literal "en-US".

findings.title: Unnecessary blanket UPDATE of all SelectedCalendars on every cache fill
findings.body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` issues an `UPDATE "SelectedCalendar" SET "updatedAt" = now() WHERE credentialId = ?` for every credential each time availability is cached (including on every Google webhook). The PR description itself states `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not consumed anywhere in the UI (the UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache), so this is a write with no reader that adds row churn and lock contention on a hot path. For delegation credentials (negative in-memory id) it also matches nothing. Remove it or document a concrete consumer.

findings.title: Cache status query bypasses the calendar-cache feature check
findings.body: The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of going through the `CalendarCache` factory that returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the feature is disabled. As a result every `connectedCalendars` request performs an extra `groupBy` on CalendarCache even for users/teams without calendar cache enabled, and stale rows left over from a previously enabled feature are surfaced in the UI as an active cache (with a delete action) even though caching is off.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt
findings.body: The query filters only on `credentialId in (...)`, so expired cache rows (`expiresAt < now()`) are reported with their `_max(updatedAt)`. The UI then shows "Cache Status – Last updated: …" for a cache that will never be served, misleading the user about whether the credential is actually cached. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` (or expose expiry so the UI can label stale caches).

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId that the function never uses
findings.body: `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` were widened to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, but neither field is read anywhere in this file. Because `UserWithCalendars` is the public input type of `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` (also re-exported as `getConnectedDestinationCalendars` for `@calcom/platform-libraries`), every external caller that selects only `externalId/integration/eventTypeId` now fails type-checking and must be updated (only `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated in this PR). Revert the widening unless the fields are actually needed.

findings.title: Migration backfills updatedAt with NOW(), making stale caches look fresh
findings.body: All pre-existing CalendarCache rows get `updatedAt = <migration time>`. The new UI reads this value and renders "Last updated: <timestamp>", so immediately after deploy every existing cache — including ones written weeks ago — appears to have been refreshed at deploy time. Consider backfilling from a better proxy (e.g. `expiresAt - CACHING_TIME`) or making the column nullable so "unknown" can be shown. Also the auto-generated warning block ("Added the required column `updatedAt` ... without a default value") contradicts the statement actually executed, which does specify a default.

findings.title: Dev script is macOS-only and writes to a path outside the repo
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax; on Linux (GNU sed) the empty string is interpreted as the script argument and the command fails with "unknown command", leaving GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL unchanged while the script still prints the success message. Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory, so running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root creates/edits a `.env` in the repo's parent directory rather than the project one. Resolve the path relative to the script location and use a portable in-place edit.

findings.title: dev:cron depends on tsx which is not a declared dependency
findings.body: `dev:cron` was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`. `tsx` is not in dependencies/devDependencies, so `npx` will attempt an interactive network install on each fresh environment (and fail in offline/CI contexts), while the now-unused `ts-node` devDependency remains. Add `tsx` as a devDependency and invoke it without `npx`.

findings.title: No tests for the new deleteCache handler or getCacheStatusByCredentialIds
findings.body: This PR adds a destructive mutation (`viewer.calendars.deleteCache`) with hand-rolled authorization and a new repository read (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), but no unit tests. At minimum there should be tests asserting that (a) a credential belonging to another user cannot have its cache deleted, (b) the matching CalendarCache rows are removed for an owned credential, and (c) the status aggregation returns the max updatedAt per credentialId and an empty result for unknown ids.
